answer.evidence: The Halstead conversion is in radon/metrics.py, `halstead_visitor_report`. Line 79 guards volume with `if h != 0`. Line 80 guards difficulty with `if h2 != 0`. Effort is difficulty*volume (line 81), time is effort/18.0 (line 93) and bugs is volume/3000.0 (line 94). The zero-count cases are covered for h, h2 and volume. I did not read the length calculation at line 76 closely. It calls `math.log(h1, 2)` and `math.log(h2, 2)`, so I would check that the lines above it guard h1 == 0 and h2 == 0. `mi_compute` (lines 98-117) returns early when volume or sloc is <= 0, so `math.log` never gets a non-positive argument. The cyclomatic complexity value is also an input to the maintainability index (line 98), so I'd check how radon/complexity.py produces and aggregates it, including the zero or empty-module case. I'd also check the line counts in radon/raw.py, since sloc and comment counts feed the same formula (lines 98 and 136). The visitor code in radon/visitors.py that collects operators and operands gets a shorter pass. I planned the time by risk and haven't run the code or tests yet, so none of this is verified by execution.
